_doc: Large batch L10 themed pass (TEMPLATE.md sections 9 and 10): tide crab knight and paladin, mangrove crab king and emperor, coconut crab youngster, clam lurker, giant clam. New motifs live in motifs/large_L10.js (37, glyph/motion ids prefixed L10-; all 7 signatures bring a custom chain effect: knight fencing footwork, paladin marching under its banner, king's procession sprouting prop-root arches, emperor trailing a train of roots, youngster tottering under its husk hat, clam lurker ploughing a sand bulge, giant clam's clap sending a wave crest along). Every creature has its own signature motif and keeps it exclusive (7 of 7). Sibling shares only where the picture is the same: gauntlet-slam (knight -> paladin Crusader Bash, gold), hammer-claw, prop-root, royal-pincer, mire-grab and mud-armour (king <-> emperor), siphon-spray, pearl-glint, undertow-swirl, shell-gate and sealed-valve (clam lurker <-> giant clam), sidestep-crab (knight and king scuttles). Reused from earlier batches where truly the same: medium surf-foam (breakers; the youngster's Night-Shift Splash adds the moon), crab-clamp (one big claw), coconut-crack (robber crab = coconut crab), large barnacle-cone (paladin barnacle armour), small mud-flop (mangrove spatter). Every piece (unique, class and x0) has a hand note. Sonnet's flagged piece coconut-crab-youngster/f:u1 Husk Hide is drawn as the husk-hide motif (the crab ducking under its husk, eyestalks peeking) scattering out and back.

tide-crab-knight.notes: The grown-up tide crab squire: a sea-blue shore crab knight in shell plate mail that fences with its slender claw like a rapier, jousts down the beach and throws down its gauntlet to call a duel. Slides in sideways like a crab fencer.

b0.n: Duelling Pincer: blade claws lunge en garde off the edge, thrust with a white glint at the tip and recover

b1.n: Breaker Splash: sea-blue breakers curl off the edge and burst into white spray

b2.n: Shell Plate Mail: overlapping shell plates line the edge in three courses, rivets shining, a sheen stepping across

b3.n: Retreat Scuttle: knights back off sideways at spots, claws raised in guard, tied by sand-scrape lines, dust kicked up

x0.n: Gauntlet Slam: armoured claw fists rise and slam down off the edge, cracks running out, dust jumping

u0.n: Knight's Claw: a rapier claw runs the length of the edge in a fencer's lunge; the chain is the knight advancing in footwork, a half step back between steps

u1.n: Tide Shield: round shell shields with a wave-crest blazon lock along the edge, the tide sheeting over them in drops

u2.n: Joust: crabs charge out of the edge with their long lance claws couched, pennants snapping, and drop back

u3.n: Duel Call: a gauntlet is thrown down at spot after spot, tumbling, a challenge mark flashing, the spots tied together

tide-crab-paladin.notes: A teal island tide crab in barnacle armour that holds one claw up as a banner pole: a holy shore warrior with a haloed pincer, a hooked shield and spiked pauldrons. Lands heavy like a knight in full plate.

b0.n: Holy Pincer: pincers snap off the edge under small gold halos, a sparkle at each snap

b1.n: Banner Spray: banners whip off the edge flinging sea spray from the cloth

b2.n: Barnacle Plate: pale barnacle cones crust the edge like armour, lids opening and cirri combing out

b3.n: Shoreline Trip: a tideline of kelp wrack with shells caught in it is strung from spot to spot to trip on

x0.n: Crusader Bash: gold armoured fists slam down off the edge, cracks running out

u0.n: Pauldron Spike: barnacled shoulder plates push out of the edge, three steel spikes growing from each

u1.n: Shield Hook: a hooked claw reaches out from behind a round shield, catches and yanks back

u2.n: Tide Banner: banners are planted at spots tied by a tide line, pennants snapping; the chain is the paladin marching under its banner, prints behind, a gold flash where it plants it

u3.n: Oath Strike: a claw rises straight up under gold rays as an oath, then smashes down in a white flash, rings spreading

mangrove-crab-king.notes: The olive mangrove crab grown into a king: holds court under the arching prop roots of the mangrove in a little gold crown, wears mud as armour and snatches from the mire. Steps up in a stately procession.

b0.n: Mangrove Pincer: olive claws lunge off the edge and snap, mud clods flying

b1.n: Mangrove Spatter: mud splats flop off the edge and drop into a dark pool

b2.n: Mangrove Shell: the king sits back under its prop-root arch along the edge, crown glinting

b3.n: Mangrove Scuttle: crabs scuttle sideways out between the roots and back, mud kicked up

x0.n: Mangrove Hammer: a mallet crusher claw swings out and smashes down, mud clods flying

u0.n: Root Grip: prop roots arch up at spots tied together and curl their tips down to grip

u1.n: King's Pincer: the king's signet-banded pincer runs the length of the edge, opening and snapping

u2.n: Mud Armour: mud-daubed shells hold along the edge, the mud plates running off in drips

u3.n: Mud Snatch: mud pools hang at spots tied together; a claw rises out of each and snaps shut, mud flicking

mangrove-crab-emperor.notes: The mangrove king's elder: a vast gold-edged crab wearing a crown of living mangrove roots, drinking brine as a tonic and cloaking itself in roots. Trundles in slowly with all its weight.

b0.n: Imperial Pinch: gold signet pincers lunge off the edge and snap

b1.n: Imperial Wave: claws rise off the edge in a slow regal wave, ripple rings spreading under them

b2.n: Imperial Mudcoat: gold shells coated in mud hold along the edge, the mud dripping into dark pools

b3.n: Imperial Mire: mire pools at spots tied together, a gold claw rising out of each and snatching

x0.n: Imperial Smash: gold crusher claws smash down off the edge, mud and dust flying

u0.n: Imperial Claw: the root-crowned emperor rears out of the edge and slams down; the chain is the emperor trundling on with a train of twisting roots and gold glints

u1.n: Brine Tonic: gold-rimmed shell cups brimming with brine rise off the edge, bubbles climbing, a mangrove leaf on each

u2.n: Root Cloak: prop roots push out of the edge like a cloak of spikes, leaves on top

u3.n: Shell Lock: gold-rimmed shell halves close along the edge and lock with a steel cross clasp, a glint

coconut-crab-youngster.notes: A half-size blue-purple coconut crab still learning the trade: wears a coconut husk on its head like a hat that keeps slipping over its eyes, practises its pinch on nuts that will not crack and works the night shift on the beach. Rolls in, clumsy.

b0.n: Pincer Practice: small purple claws snap off the edge, whiffing at air, until one finally hits

b1.n: Night-Shift Splash: night wavelets curl off the edge under a moon glint and break into spray

b2.n: Half-Grown Husk: husks sit along the edge with the youngster tucked under each, eyestalks peeking

b3.n: Scuttle Sidle: the youngster sidles out and back with its husk hat wobbling, sand dust behind

x0.n: Apprentice Slam: coconuts slam down off the edge and at last crack open, white flesh showing

u0.n: Husk Snip: little claws snip at husk lumps off the edge, coir fibres flying

u1.n: Husk Hide: husks skitter out and back with the youngster ducked under them, eyestalks popping up and down

u2.n: Husk Toss: husks are tossed end over end onto spots tied together by coir fibres

u3.n: Hat Bonk: the youngster charges out head first and its husk hat bonks down over its eyes; the chain is it tottering on, the husk slipping halfway

clam-lurker.notes: A mottled clam that lies half buried in the coast sand, opening a crack to peer out with rows of blue mantle eyes and snapping shut on whatever steps near; spits, slimes and pulls with the undertow. Rises out of the ground.

b0.n: Gate Clamp: ridged valves swing out of the edge like gates and slam shut with white streaks

b1.n: Yawning Spray: siphon tubes jet lines of spray off the edge that fan out at the end

b2.n: Slimy Mantle: frilled mantle lips line the edge, slime strands stretching and drops letting go

b3.n: Gulping Pull: a half-buried clam pops up at spot after spot and gulps, sand sucked into its gape

x0.n: Shutter Thump: whole clams heave up out of the sand and thump back down shut, sand puffing

u0.n: Clamp: buried clams lie in wait at spots tied together, open a crack with blue eyes peering, and snap shut; the chain is a sand bulge ploughing to the next piece

u1.n: Shut Tight: ridged clams lie shut along the edge, the seam locked, pressure ticks pulsing at the ends

u2.n: Pearl Glint: an opened shell shows its pearl at spot after spot, the glint flaring to a four-ray blaze

u3.n: Clam Undertow: undertow spirals turn at spots tied together, sand grains drawn in, bubbles rising

giant-clam.notes: A cart-sized island clam with wavy ridged grey valves and a wide pale mouth of glossy teal mantle; it never moves, it just claps shut with a boom that sends the water running. Drops onto its spot with a splash ring.

b0.n: Giant Sudden Shut: huge grey valves swing off the edge and slam shut like gates

b1.n: Shallow Spurt: wide siphons spurt water off the edge in the shallows, bubbles rising

b2.n: Glossy Mantle: the wavy mantle lip lines the edge, iridescent spots shimmering teal, blue and violet

b3.n: Tidal Suck: tidal spirals turn at spots tied together, pulling sand into the clam

x0.n: Cart-Size Clap: the giant valves heave out, gape on the teal mantle and clap shut with a white burst

u0.n: Slam Shut: a giant clam slams shut down the length of the edge; the chain is its clap sending a foaming wave crest along to the next piece

u1.n: Pearl Blind: pearls flash out and back in a blinding four-ray blaze, white glints scattering

u2.n: Shell Wall: giant ridged shells lie shut along the edge like a wall, pressure ticks at the seams

u3.n: Sudden Shut: valve tips smack together off the edge, a jagged shock bursting from the join, spray flying
